_about: Portfolio cut (85-95 s) of the WhatsApp Commerce V2 video, built by bin/demo (see README.md). Spoken text is spelled out for speech; every claim traces to docs/evidence/PORTFOLIO_CLAIMS.md and the verification write-ups. Segment 02-demo shows SYNTHETIC data (a local database, same code, Meta replaced by an in-process fake): it opens with an 'Application demo · synthetic data' card and every local frame carries a small DEMO DATA tag. b03 shows the author's real WhatsApp screenshots (7 Oct 2026, shown as crops, never edited); b10-b11 are real verification evidence (6 Oct 2026). A beat's min_seconds keeps its picture on screen at least that long. Voice: Kokoro-82M af_heart at speed 0.95.

beats.text: Version one dropped every delivery status and hid its errors.

beats.visual: real WhatsApp screenshots (7 Oct 2026): Hi and catalog card; catalog and product; cart, sent cart and receipt
beats.text: First, a real conversation. The customer says hi and gets a catalog card. They browse the catalog inside WhatsApp, build a cart and send it. A receipt comes straight back.

beats.visual: how it works: WhatsApp, webhook, persist, queue, process, order validation, reply and status tracking
beats.text: Behind it, every webhook is verified, stored and acknowledged, then processed once in the background, and every reply is tracked.

beats.visual: application demo card (synthetic data), then the operator's conversation view for the synthetic hero customer
beats.text: Now the operator's view, with demo data: Maya says hi and sends her cart.

beats.visual: order detail: lines, customer price vs catalog price, total
beats.text: Each line is checked against the catalog price.

beats.visual: order accepted + notification sent, delivered, read timestamps
beats.text: Once accepted, the reply is tracked by the statuses Meta sends back: sent, delivered, read.

beats.visual: deliveries list + a delivery with a duplicate outcome
beats.text: Duplicates are ignored, and stored deliveries can be replayed safely.

beats.visual: health page: failures by category, unknown outcome never resent
beats.text: Failures stay visible, and an ambiguous send is never resent.
On October sixth it ran against real Meta traffic, and every delivery was applied once.

beats.visual: 131009 card: Meta's stored details, cause in the commerce settings, fixed in Meta
beats.text: The first catalog card failed: error one three one, zero zero nine. Its stored details pointed to a commerce setting. Fixed by hand in Meta, the next message went through.
Eleven hundred and twelve tests pass, with security scans in CI, and it's deployed over HTTPS with a tested restore.

beats.visual: closing card with the limits and the repository
